metaTitle: Best Dinnerware Sets With Mugs in 2026
metaDescription: Five dinnerware sets that include mugs compared by plate size, mug capacity, material and care, from 16-piece stoneware to a 30-piece porcelain service.
introParagraphs: A dinnerware set that includes mugs saves you from matching cups to plates later, and it means coffee and soup are served in pieces that belong together. This guide compares five sets with mugs: the Gibson Elite Soho Lounge 16-piece stoneware set, the Gibson Home Ogalla 30-piece porcelain set for six, the Gibson Home Zuma 16-piece matte black stoneware set, the Famiware Star 16-piece reactive glaze set, and the Pfaltzgraff Gabriela Blue 16-piece stoneware set.

The mug itself varies more than you might expect. The Gibson Zuma includes 16 ounce mugs, the Soho Lounge includes 13.5 ounce mugs, and the Ogalla adds six mugs to a larger service for six. Dinner plates range from 10.5 inches to 11 inches, and three of the five sets are stoneware while the Ogalla is white porcelain with a gold band.

We evaluated each set based on product specs and buyer feedback, with attention to mug capacity, plate and bowl mix, care instructions and how heavy the pieces are to handle. We do not claim lab testing, and where a listing leaves out care details we say so.

products.name: Gibson Elite Soho Lounge 16-Piece Stoneware Set
products.description:
The Gibson Elite Soho Lounge is a service for four with 11 inch dinner plates, 7.95 inch dessert plates, 5.5 inch bowls and 13.5 ounce mugs. The double reactive glaze gives each piece a dreamlike, varied color. It is the one set here where the listing says both dishwasher and microwave safe without caveats.

The 11 inch dinner plate is the largest in this guide, so it holds a full meal comfortably. The tradeoff is that stoneware is heavier than porcelain, and the 5.5 inch bowl is small for soup. Because the glaze varies, no two pieces match exactly.

Care is easy given the stated dishwasher and microwave safety, and 16 pieces store in a compact stack. Compared with the Gibson Zuma, the Soho Lounge has a smaller 13.5 ounce mug but a bigger dinner plate. It is a good all around set for a couple or a small family.
products.bestFor: Couples and small families who want a stoneware set with mugs and clear dishwasher and microwave guidance
pros: Largest 11 inch dinner plate in this guide
Dishwasher and microwave safe per listing
cons: 5.5 inch bowl is small for soup

products.name: Gibson Home Ogalla 30-Piece Porcelain Set With Mugs for 6
products.description:
The Gibson Home Ogalla gives six people five pieces each, including mugs, for 30 pieces in total. It includes six 10.5 inch dinner plates, six 7.5 inch dessert plates, six 6 inch cereal bowls and more. The white porcelain has a gold band and curved contours that give it a dressier look.

The tradeoff is the gold trim, which usually means the pieces should stay out of the microwave, and the listing text we reviewed does not give care instructions. Thirty pieces also take serious cabinet space.

Gibson is a family of brands the listing describes as having over 40 years of expertise in home dining. Compared with the Soho Lounge, the Ogalla serves two more people and costs less but is lighter and more formal. Treat it as a dining table set rather than a microwave workhorse.

products.name: Gibson Home Zuma 16-Piece Matte Black Stoneware Set
products.description:
The Gibson Home Zuma is a matte black stoneware service for four with 10.5 inch dinner plates, 8 inch dessert plates, 6.3 inch bowls holding 28 ounces and 16 ounce mugs. A soft matte glaze with an off-white lip along the rim creates a sleek look. The 16 ounce mug is the largest in this comparison.

Big mugs suit coffee drinkers and anyone who likes soup in a mug. The tradeoff is that matte black shows scuffs and water spots more than light glazes, and stoneware is heavier than porcelain. The soft lip edges are meant to feel pleasant at the rim.

Storage is compact with 16 pieces, and the solid color is easy to mix with other black or white pieces. The listing does not give dishwasher or microwave details in the text we reviewed, so check the box. Compared with the Soho Lounge, the Zuma has bigger mugs and a deeper bowl, but a smaller dinner plate.
products.bestFor: Coffee and soup lovers who want large mugs and deep bowls in a modern black set
pros: 16 ounce mugs are the biggest here
Matte glaze with soft lip edge

Care guidance not stated in the listing

products.name: Famiware Star 16-Piece Stoneware Set With Mugs
products.description:
The Famiware Star is a stoneware set with mugs, plates and bowls for four people. The listing says it is made from natural clay with a lead free and cadmium free glaze and a handcrafted double reactive glaze. It was fired at 2340 degrees Fahrenheit for 13.5 hours.

The high firing means solid weight and thickness, which the listing says resists chipping. The handcrafted glaze means each piece is unique.

The listing text does not give plate or mug sizes, so you cannot compare capacity against the Gibson sets. Storage is compact at 16 pieces. If you want a styled stoneware set with written glaze safety claims, this one fits, whereas the Ogalla is the better value.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want styled stoneware with stated lead and cadmium free glaze and mugs for four
pros: Lead and cadmium free glaze stated
Solid weight from high temperature firing
cons: Listing gives no plate or mug sizes

products.name: Pfaltzgraff Gabriela Blue 16-Piece Stoneware Set
products.description:
The Pfaltzgraff Gabriela Blue is a 16-piece stoneware service for four with 10.5 inch dinner plates, 8.5 inch salad plates, 6 inch bowls and mugs. A blue floral border garland gives it a traditional, patterned look. The reactive glaze finish on the exterior adds depth.

This is the set for people who prefer traditional pattern over a modern solid color. The tradeoff is that busy patterns date faster than plain glazes, and the listing text we reviewed does not give mug capacity.

The stoneware is described as durable enough for daily use. Compared with the Zuma, it has a gentler look and smaller bowls. Check the box for dishwasher and microwave details before use.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prefer a traditional blue floral pattern in a stoneware set with mugs
pros: Blue floral border adds traditional charm
cons: Patterned look may not suit modern decor

buyingCriteria.explanation: Mug size varies, with the Gibson Zuma offering 16 ounce mugs and the Soho Lounge offering 13.5 ounce mugs. The Ogalla includes six mugs but the listing text does not state capacity. A 12 ounce mug fits a standard coffee, while 16 ounces suits soup or large lattes. Pick the size that matches how you actually use mugs.

The Soho Lounge has an 11 inch dinner plate and the Zuma has a 6.3 inch bowl at 28 ounces. The Ogalla and Gabriela both use 10.5 inch dinner plates. Bigger plates hold full meals but are heavier to wash. A bowl under 6 inches is small for soup.

Stoneware, as in the Soho Lounge, Zuma, Famiware Star and Gabriela, is sturdy and heavier. Porcelain, as in the Ogalla, is lighter. If you lift stacks often, choose porcelain. For a robust daily feel, stoneware is fine.

The Soho Lounge lists dishwasher and microwave safety. The Ogalla has a gold band, and metal trim usually means no microwave. Check the label for every set. When guidance is missing, hand wash the first time.

The Famiware Star states lead and cadmium free glaze. FDA sets leach limits for ceramic dinnerware, so written statements are useful. Other listings say less, so check the packaging. Be cautious with decorative glazes.

Most sets here are 16 pieces for four, while the Ogalla is 30 pieces for six. If you host often, the larger set saves a second purchase. Count how many people drink coffee at your table. Extra mugs are handy for guests.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mug and plate sizing
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the stated mug capacities and plate sizes. The Zuma has the biggest mug at 16 ounces and the Soho Lounge has the largest plate at 11 inches. Sets that gave no sizes scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at stoneware versus porcelain and the firing details. The Ogalla is the only porcelain set, and the Famiware Star details high temperature firing. We scored lighter sets higher on handling. The strongest on weight is the Ogalla and the most basic is stoneware.

howWeEvaluated.title: Care guidance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for dishwasher and microwave statements. The Soho Lounge was clearest. The Ogalla's gold band suggests limits. Clear care earns credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Completeness
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted pieces and mugs per person. The Ogalla offers six settings with mugs, while the others offer four. Sets that include all four pieces per seat scored well. We noted missing sizes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: The Ogalla is lowest cost and Famiware Star is highest. We scored value by pieces per cost. Written safety claims added credit.

faq.q: Why buy a dinnerware set that includes mugs?
faq.a: A set with mugs ensures your cups match your plates and bowls. It also saves a separate purchase. Sets like the Soho Lounge and Zuma include mugs in the 16 pieces.

faq.q: How do I choose between stoneware and porcelain?
faq.a: Stoneware is sturdy and heavier, while porcelain is lighter and more formal. The Ogalla is porcelain and the other four are stoneware. Choose based on how much weight you want to lift.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a set with mugs?
faq.a: In our data the Ogalla is the lowest cost and the Famiware Star is the highest. More pieces do not always cost more. Choose the set that fits your table.

faq.q: Can I put the mugs in the microwave?
faq.a: The Soho Lounge lists microwave safety. The Ogalla's gold band suggests avoiding the microwave. Check the label for every set.
A 12 ounce mug fits standard coffee, while 16 ounces suits soup or large drinks. The Zuma has 16 ounce mugs and the Soho Lounge has 13.5 ounce mugs. Choose by habit.

faq.q: Are matte glazes harder to clean?
faq.a: Matte glazes can show scuffs and water spots more than gloss glazes. The Zuma uses a matte glaze. Wash promptly to keep it looking clean.
